subtitle: In the thin air of Ladakh, a single house learns how not to break

panels.shot: wide cinematic panorama of a Ladakhi village clinging to terraced fields beneath stark brown mountains and a glacier-fed stream
panels.action: Khangchen Heir of Ladakh stands on a flat rooftop above clustered whitewashed houses and golden barley terraces, wrapped in thick wool, gazing over canals, fields and a distant monastery perched on a ridge.

dialogue.text: Between desert rock and snow peaks, Ladakhi khangchen households chose one marriage, one house, and one field to keep their land whole.

i18n.hi: रेगिस्तानी चट्टान और बर्फ़ीली चोटियों के बीच, लद्दाखी खांगचेन घरानों ने एक शादी, एक घर, एक खेत चुनकर ज़मीन जोड़ी रखी

panels.shot: slow push-in from high aerial view to a single irrigated strip-field glowing against surrounding barren slopes
panels.action: From above, the village’s narrow green fields shine like ribbons along a single canal, surrounded by vast grey-brown mountains and empty scree, as Khangchen Heir of Ladakh walks the field edge with a wooden ploughshare on his shoulder.

dialogue.text: In Ladakh, water came in one thin line, and life clung to that line. Beyond the last field, there was only stone and wind.

i18n.hi: लद्दाख में पानी बस एक पतली धार था, ज़िंदगी उसी से लटकी थी। आख़िरी खेत के पार बस पत्थर और हवा थी

panels.shot: medium close-up at field level, camera low so canal and earth fill the frame
panels.action: Khangchen Heir of Ladakh kneels beside a narrow irrigation channel, letting meltwater run through his fingers as terraced plots step down behind him and snow peaks glint far away.

dialogue.text: Irrigated land could not be stretched, and harvests were narrow. Yet royal scribes still counted grain, animals and men for tax and corvée.

i18n.hi: सिंचित ज़मीन फैल नहीं सकती थी, फसल भी कम थी। फिर भी दरबारी लेखक टैक्स और बेगार के लिए अनाज, मवेशी और मर्द गिनते रहे

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a thick-walled Ladakhi room lit by butter lamps and a central skylight
panels.action: Inside a spacious khangchen hall with carved pillars and low hearth, Khangchen Heir of Ladakh sits with an older couple and two younger men, all around stacked grain bins and wool sacks, while snow gathers outside a small window.

dialogue.text: Villagers called the big houses khangchen. They were not only walls and roofs, but fields, animals, tools, men and women counted together as one unit.

i18n.hi: गाँव वाले बड़े घरों को खांगचेन कहते थे। वे सिर्फ़ दीवारें नहीं, बल्कि खेत, जानवर, औज़ार, औरत-मर्द सब मिलकर एक इकाई थे

panels.shot: diagrammatic overhead-style shot of a courtyard where lines in the dust mark imagined divisions of fields and buildings
panels.action: In the courtyard, Khangchen Heir of Ladakh scratches lines in the dust, dividing a simple rectangle into many thin strips as worried family members look on and the farmhouse, cowshed and stacked hay loom behind them.

dialogue.text: If each son took a share, the big house would splinter. A plough-team, a canal right, a threshing floor—none could be split forever and still feed all.

i18n.hi: अगर हर बेटा हिस्सा बाँट लेता, बड़ा घर बिखर जाता। हल की जोड़ी, नहर का हक, खलिहान—कुछ भी बाँटते-बाँटते सबको नहीं पाल पाते

panels.shot: medium shot of the parents and sons facing each other across the hearth
panels.action: By the warm glow of the hearth, an elderly couple sits opposite two grown sons and Khangchen Heir of Ladakh, their faces serious as they gesture to the grain bins and a wooden tally board.

dialogue.text: The problem was simple, and heavy. How many married couples could one field support? Where would the younger brothers go?

i18n.hi: सवाल सीधा था, पर भारी। एक खेत कितने शादीशुदा जोड़े सँभाले? छोटे भाई कहाँ जाएँ?

panels.shot: flashback-style shot with slightly desaturated tones, showing a village assembly outdoors
panels.action: On a windswept flat near the village, elders in thick woolen robes and felt boots sit in a circle, as Khangchen Heir of Ladakh listens; behind them, the outline of a royal fortress and a monastery crown distant ridges.

dialogue.text: Over generations, Ladakhi villagers and rulers shaped an answer. They kept the house whole, and changed the ways brothers and sons lived within it.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी, लद्दाख के गाँवों और राजाओं ने जवाब गढ़ा। घर को पूरा रखा, और भाइयों-बेटों की ज़िंदगी घर के भीतर बदल दी

panels.shot: intimate interior shot focused on a marriage scene in the same big house
panels.action: In the decorated main room, a bride in layered robes and turquoise headdress sits between two brothers, while Khangchen Heir of Ladakh looks on; elders pour chang and young women carry bread and butter tea.

dialogue.text: In many khangchen, brothers took one wife together. Fraternal polyandry tied all male heirs to the same marriage, the same hearth, the same inheritance.

i18n.hi: कई खांगचेन में भाई मिलकर एक ही पत्नी लेते थे। भ्रातृ बहुपतित्‍व से सारे वारिस एक ही शादी, एक ही चूल्हे, एक ही विरासत में बँध जाते

panels.shot: medium close-up of the bride and the eldest brother, with the younger brother slightly behind
panels.action: Khangchen Heir of Ladakh, as eldest brother, sits closest to the bride, his hand resting near hers, while the younger brother sits just behind his shoulder, respectful yet included in the scene.

dialogue.speaker: ladakhi_khangchen_households
dialogue.text: The house will stay one, and we will share the work.

i18n.hi: घर एक रहेगा, और काम हम सब बाँटेंगे

panels.shot: montage-style split frame showing work in different seasons
panels.action: A composite image shows Khangchen Heir of Ladakh and his brother ploughing with yaks in spring, cutting barley in autumn, and repairing the roof in winter, while the same bride tends animals and kneads dough by the hearth.

dialogue.text: Anthropologists later noted how this shared marriage matched land and labor. Two or three brothers, one wife, one set of fields, one tax bill paid.

i18n.hi: बाद में मानवशास्त्रियों ने नोट किया कि ये साझा शादी ज़मीन और मज़दूरी से कितनी जमी। दो-तीन भाई, एक पत्नी, एक खेतों का सेट, एक ही टैक्स चुकाया

panels.shot: wider village shot contrasting two houses, one large and one smaller
panels.action: In the village street, Khangchen Heir of Ladakh passes a towering big house with many prayer flags, then a modest two-room dwelling where a single couple stacks fuel outside, smoke rising from a small chimney.

dialogue.text: Yet not every family lived this way. Some small households split, others married sons out, and customs shifted with status, village and time.

i18n.hi: पर हर परिवार ऐसा नहीं रहता था। कुछ छोटे घर टूटे, कुछ ने बेटों की शादी बाहर की, और रिवाज़ जात, गाँव, समय के साथ बदलते रहे

panels.shot: interior of a monastery courtyard overlooking the valley, with novices and monks in red robes
panels.action: In a sunlit monastery courtyard above the village, young boys in maroon robes sweep and study, while older monks chant; Khangchen Heir of Ladakh stands at the gate, watching a younger brother bow to the abbot.

dialogue.text: Another path led upward, to monasteries. Many younger sons took vows, trading inheritance for script, ritual and the monastery’s steady bowl of tsampa.

i18n.hi: एक और राह ऊपर मठों को जाती थी। कई छोटे भाइयों ने दीक्षा ली, विरासत छोड़कर लिखत, पूजा और मठ की स्थिर त्साम्पा की कटोरी चुन ली

panels.shot: medium close-up on the younger brother’s shaven head and new maroon robe, with the family in the background
panels.action: The younger brother, head newly shaven, adjusts his maroon robe as he looks back once at his family—Khangchen Heir of Ladakh and their parents standing below, hands joined in a quiet farewell.

dialogue.speaker: ladakhi_khangchen_households
dialogue.text: His share is prayer and learning; mine is field and house.

i18n.hi: उसका हिस्सा प्रार्थना और पढ़ाई है; मेरा खेत और घर

panels.shot: interior monastery library shot with shelves of pecha manuscripts and herbal medicines
panels.action: Inside a dim monastery room lined with pecha manuscripts and bundles of dried herbs, a monk brother grinds medicine while another reads aloud, as villagers wait quietly in the doorway; Khangchen Heir of Ladakh stands among them with a cap in his hands.

dialogue.text: Monasteries did more than thin inheritance. They taught letters, healed with herbs, timed irrigation by stars, and settled quarrels when village law ran thin.

i18n.hi: मठों ने सिर्फ़ विरासत नहीं घटाई। वे अक्षर सिखाते, जड़ी-बूटियों से इलाज करते, तारों से सिंचाई की घड़ी देखते, और जब गाँव का क़ानून हल्का पड़ता तो झगड़े सुलझाते

panels.shot: village council scene under a clear sky with mountains in the background
panels.action: On the village threshing ground, elders sit in a rough circle, a monk and a lay official among them, as Khangchen Heir of Ladakh and another villager present a dispute about a crumbling field wall.

dialogue.text: Customary law, village councils and royal orders met in these open spaces. Together they decided who kept a field, who entered a khangchen, who left for another life.

i18n.hi: रिवाज़ी क़ानून, गाँव की पंचायत और शाही हुक्म इन्हीं चौपालों में मिलते। यहीं तय होता कौन खेत रखे, कौन खांगचेन में घुसे, कौन दूसरी ज़िंदगी की राह पकड़े

panels.shot: long shot of Leh or a similar town with a palace-fort and a monastery above clustered houses
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view shows Leh’s palace rising over flat-roofed houses and a monastery, as caravans snake along the valley floor; inset closer, Khangchen Heir of Ladakh stands before a tax official with a small sack of grain and a yak tethered nearby.

dialogue.text: From the Namgyal court to the smallest hamlet, the state leaned on khangchen households. Taxes, corvée labor, and caravan duties all assumed fields stayed undivided and houses stayed strong.

i18n.hi: नमग्याल दरबार से छोटे से छोटे गाँव तक, राज्य खांगचेन घरानों पर टिका था। टैक्स, बेगार, और काफ़िले की ड्यूटी—सब मानते थे खेत नहीं टूटेंगे, घर मज़बूत रहेंगे

panels.shot: interior shot at night with family gathered as an elder reads or recites by butter lamp
panels.action: At night in the khangchen hall, an elder traces lines on a board showing family ties, while Khangchen Heir of Ladakh and younger kin listen closely, the butter lamp casting long shadows on stacked grain and harnesses.

dialogue.text: Household rules were remembered in story and practice. Who married in, who became monk, who went as foster or servant—each choice weighed land, water, and the house’s future.

i18n.hi: घर के नियम कहानी और आदत में याद रखे जाते। कौन बहू बनकर आए, कौन भिक्षु बने, कौन पालने या नौकर बनकर जाए—हर फ़ैसला ज़मीन, पानी और घर के कल को तौलकर होता

panels.shot: time-lapse style composition showing the same house across decades, with subtle changes in clothing and surroundings
panels.action: A composite panel shows the same khangchen over decades: in one layer Khangchen Heir of Ladakh as a young man, in another as an elder with grandchildren, prayer flags fading and renewed, fields steady below.

dialogue.text: Across the 1600s and 1700s, through trade booms and border wars, many big houses endured. Their inner arrangements shifted, but the irrigated plots below their walls stayed one.

i18n.hi: सत्रहवीं-अठारहवीं सदी के व्यापार उछाल और सरहदी लड़ाइयों के बीच, कई बड़े घर टिके रहे। भीतर की व्यवस्थाएँ बदलीं, पर उनकी दीवारों के नीचे के सिंचित टुकड़े जुड़े रहे

panels.shot: wide shot of the village and mountains at dawn, with a hint of the future in the distance
panels.action: At dawn, Khangchen Heir of Ladakh stands again on his rooftop, the village quiet below, canals glinting, while far on the horizon faint silhouettes of new-style buildings and a road hint at change to come.

dialogue.text: Today, Ladakh’s households follow many paths. Yet the old khangchen and its shared marriage, shared work and shared vows still ask us how societies bend, but do not break, when land and water cannot grow.

i18n.hi: आज लद्दाख के घर कई राहें चलते हैं। पर पुराना खांगचेन और उसकी साझा शादी, साझा मेहनत और साझा वचन अभी भी पूछते हैं: ज़मीन-पानी न बढ़ें तो समाज कैसे झुके, पर टूटे नहीं

title_i18n.en: The Mountain Household Keeps the Land Whole
title_i18n.hi: पहाड़ी घराने ने ज़मीन को पूरा रखा

subtitle_i18n.en: In the thin air of Ladakh, a single house learns how not to break
subtitle_i18n.hi: लद्दाख की पतली हवा में, एक घर सीख रहा था कैसे न टूटे
